title: Introduce evacuation grace reserve to smooth regional failovers and SLO enforcement
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: During recent regional evacuations we observed sudden, near-immediate global load-shedding spikes as nodes reclaimed capacity and regional routing switched. This caused expensive error budgets and flapping circuit states for mid-priority tenants. This PR introduces an 'evacuation grace reserve' which conservatively holds a small capacity reserve and a token-based grace budget per-region so that staged failovers preserve the highest-priority inflight work and avoid simultaneous full-shed waves. --- Design summary: Add a lightweight controller (EvacGraceReserve) that tracks regional evacuation signals and maintains a per-region reserve token pool derived from the region's current SLO headroom. When an evacuation/failover is signaled, the controller allocates tokens to steward a gradual admission taper: requests can draw a reserve token to bypass coarse load-shed gates for a bounded window. Tokens expire and are replenished on a conservative cadence. The runtime shedder integrates a non-blocking reserve consumer that prefers KV-preserving work and short-lived requests. The mechanism is opt-in via the runtime config and feature-flagged behind runtime.evacuations.grace_reserve.enabled. --- Config knobs: runtime.evacuations.grace_reserve.enabled (bool), runtime.evacuations.grace_reserve.initial_percent (string decimal, default "0.03"), runtime.evacuations.grace_reserve.max_burst_tokens (int as string), runtime.evacuations.grace_reserve.token_ttl_secs (int as string), rollout.evacuations.grace_reserve.stable_window_secs (int as string). --- Behavioral guarantees: 1) Does not increase total committed capacity: reserve is a conservative fraction of ephemeral headroom only; 2) Tokens are strictly bounded by a region-local cap; 3) Token consumption is best-effort and honored only when the global shedder would otherwise evict; 4) Failure modes: if the controller panics or is OOMed, system falls back to current shedding semantics (no tokens). --- Testing and validation: Added unit tests for token accounting, integration test that simulates a two-region failover and asserts smoother tail-latency and fewer circuit flips, and a staging canary that ran for 48 hours under synthetic traffic patterns. Telemetry: added metrics evac_reserve.tokens_allocated, evac_reserve.tokens_consumed, evac_reserve.replenish_rate and histograms for reserve-bypass latency. --- Rollout plan: 1) feature-flag disabled by default; 2) enable in staging and run 72h soak; 3) enable for 10% of region traffic with canary header; 4) expand to 50% and monitor SLOs and circuit-flip rate for 24h; 5) global on if metrics look stable. Rollback: flip feature flag off; controller will gracefully expire tokens and revert to baseline. --- Why unique: Prior work focused on reactive shedding thresholds and cooldowns. This PR adds a proactive, bounded headroom reservation tuned for evacuation windows to reduce simultaneous global shedding and improve graceful degradation behavior.

review_comments: Samir Patel: Could we avoid holding the token pool in memory per region? Consider using the existing slot-reservation service to persist token state across controller restarts. Response: We deliberately kept it ephemeral to minimize cross-region write amplification; added resilience path to reconstruct from headroom metrics on restart (see controller.go#rebuildFromMetrics).

Eve Torres: Add a guard so that tenant-priority metadata is respected when bypassing shedding (we can't let low-priority tenants jump the queue). Response: Added priority check in reserve_consumer.go; only tenants above configured threshold may consume tokens and we emit evac_reserve.token_denied metric.

Liam O'Connor: CI flake observed in TestIntegration_EvacReserve under heavy CPU; add backoff and rerun. Response: Increased test timeouts and added deterministic scheduling to reduce flakiness; CI rerun passed.
release_notes: Introduce Evacuation Grace Reserve: opt-in feature that preserves bounded capacity during regional evacuations to reduce simultaneous shedding and circuit flapping. Configurable via runtime.evacuations.grace_reserve.*.
